questions.q: The IT Act received its major amendment in —
questions.solution: The **2008 amendment** (effective 2009) added 66C identity theft, 66D cheating, 66F cyber-terrorism and CERT-In's statutory role.

questions.q: A nibble consists of how many bits?
questions.solution: A nibble is half a byte: 4 bits. A byte is 8 bits; a word is CPU-dependent (16/32/64 bits).
questions.shortcut: Nibble = half a byte = 4 bits ('nybble nibbles off half').

questions.q:
Match the Excel shortcut:
A. Ctrl+D  B. Ctrl+R  C. Ctrl+;  D. Alt+Enter
options: A-fill right, B-fill down, C-current time, D-new line in cell
A-fill down, B-fill right, C-current date, D-new line in cell
A-fill down, B-new line in cell, C-current date, D-fill right
A-current date, B-fill right, C-fill down, D-new line in cell
questions.solution: **D down, R right, ; date, Alt+Enter line-break.**

questions.q: The keyboard shortcut for Italics in MS Word is —
questions.solution: **Ctrl+I = Italic**; Ctrl+K inserts a hyperlink, Ctrl+J justifies, Ctrl+P prints.

questions.q:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

Mother said to me, "Do not go out in the rain."
options: Mother said me not to go out in the rain.
Mother told me to not going out in the rain.
Mother told me don't go out in the rain.
Mother told me not to go out in the rain.
questions.solution: Negative command → **told + object + not to + V1**. B uses 'said me'; C breaks the to-structure; D keeps the direct form 'don't'.
questions.shortcut: Negative order skeleton: told + me + not to + go.

questions.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
options: and long walks in the park.
questions.solution: After **enjoys**, every item takes the -ing shape: cooking, **gardening**, and (taking) long walks. 'To garden' is the odd form out.
questions.shortcut: enjoy + -ing for every item in the list.

questions.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number (4).
questions.solution: The list that follows — lighter steps, deeper sleep, steadier mood — names changes the walker actually feels: a regular walker begins to **experience** noticeable changes. *Abandon* and *postpone* contradict the praise, and *imagine* breaks the factual tone the passage maintains about doctors' findings.
questions.shortcut: Let the appositive list decide: the verb must introduce real, felt changes.
questions.passage: Every morning, before the city fully (1) ______, a quiet crowd gathers in the parks. Retired teachers, young joggers and mothers returning from the dairy booths share the same paths. The morning walk costs nothing and demands no equipment, (2) ______ very few people manage to continue it beyond a fortnight. Doctors point out that its benefits depend almost entirely on (3) ______; twenty minutes on Sunday cannot undo six days of sitting. Over the weeks, a regular walker begins to (4) ______ noticeable changes — lighter steps, deeper sleep and a steadier mood. Perhaps that is why a group that walks together (5) ______ its own quiet discipline: the ones who arrive late feel they have missed something worth keeping.

questions.q:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them contains an error. Select the part that contains the error.

The officer gave us / many useful informations / about the new scheme / and its benefits.
questions.solution: *information* is uncountable: it has no plural and cannot take *many*. Correct: **much useful information** (or *a lot of useful information*).

questions.q: Two resistors of **4 Ω and 6 Ω** are connected in series. Their total resistance is —
questions.solution: In series, resistances simply add: 4 + 6 = **10 Ω** (2.4 Ω is what a parallel combination would give).

questions.q: Which dynasty was the **first to grant tax-free land to Brahmanas**, a practice that grew in later centuries?
questions.solution: The **Satavahanas** made the first recorded **land grants to Brahmanas** — an early step towards the feudal pattern. Their inscriptions are in Prakrit; their coins were of lead and potin.

questions.q: The pH of **human blood** is about —
questions.solution: Blood is kept between 7.35 and 7.45 — **slightly basic**. 5.5 is the tooth-decay threshold; 9 is like milk of magnesia.

questions.q: The words '**socialist**, **secular**' and '**integrity**' were added to the Preamble by the —
questions.solution: The **42nd Amendment Act, 1976** (the 'Mini-Constitution') inserted socialist, secular and integrity into the Preamble. It is the only amendment the Preamble has ever received.

questions.q: 8 men or 12 boys can finish a piece of work in 10 days. 8 men and 8 boys together will finish it in:
A is 3 times as efficient as B, and together they finish a work in 12 days. A alone will finish it in:
Each interior angle of a regular octagon is:
questions.solution: ext $= \frac{360^\circ}{8} = 45^\circ$; interior $= 180^\circ - 45^\circ = 135^\circ$.
questions.shortcut: $\frac{1080}{8} = 135^\circ$ by the sum route too. Trap: $150^\circ$ (that is the dodecagon).

questions.q: Which of the following fractions gives a NON-terminating (recurring) decimal?
questions.solution:
Reduce first:
- $\frac{21}{168} = \frac{1}{8}$ → terminates.
- $\frac{33}{60} = \frac{11}{20}$ → terminates.
- $\frac{17}{125}$, $125 = 5^3$ → terminates.
- $\frac{11}{48}$, $48 = 2^4 \times 3$ → **recurring** (factor 3).
questions.shortcut: Reduce before judging: 168 contains 3 and 7, but 21/168 = 1/8.

questions.q: In a certain code language, **'sum of money' is written 'ni mo za'**; **'sum earned' is written 'mo ka'**. What is the code for of?
questions.solution: 'sum' is common → sum = mo. 'Of' can be 'ni' or 'za' — two codes remain → **cannot be determined**.

questions.q: Arrange as in a dictionary: **Melon, Melody, Mellow, Member.** Which pair sits on **adjacent** slots?
questions.solution: 4th letters: o (Melon), o (Melody), l (Mellow), b (Member) → Member, Mellow, then Melody (5th d) before Melon (5th n). Order: Member, Mellow, Melody, Melon → the last two are adjacent: **Melon and Melody**.
questions.shortcut: Write the numbered order; adjacency is just slots differing by one.

questions.q: Arrange as in a dictionary: **Angel, Angle, Anger, Amble, Amber.** Which word comes **fourth**?
questions.solution: AM group first (Amber, Amble; B < L), then the ANG group at the 4th letter: Angel (E) and Anger (E) precede Angle (L). Angel vs Anger splits at the 5th: L < R. Order: Amber, Amble, Angel, Anger, Angle → fourth = **Anger**.
questions.shortcut: First-letter split (AM/AN), then compare at the first difference only.

questions.q: Arrange as in a dictionary: **Mystery, Mystic, Myself, Myopia.** Which comes **first**?
questions.solution: MY common. 3rd letters: s (Mystery, Mystic, Myself) vs o (Myopia); o < s → **Myopia** first, whatever happens later. (Full order: Myopia, Myself, Mystery, Mystic.)
questions.shortcut: The earliest 3rd letter ends the contest at once — check the o-word first.
